technology.summary: Today's technology news includes a range of developments in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has stated that the company will not go public until it can make better promises about model safety, while BAG Ventures has raised $11.3 million to invest in AI startups. Airbnb is also launching new AI-powered services, and DoorDash is introducing text message ordering and drone deliveries. In other news, Cloudflare plans to issue quantum-safe TLS certificates, and Charter Space has raised $5 million to provide insurance for space companies. Additionally, Sonos has released the Ace Ultra headphones, and the Wing Hummingbird 7000W-B delivery drone has been unveiled.

finance.summary:
The Indian stock market is facing challenges in maintaining investor sentiment, with the Sensex and Nifty experiencing significant declines in dollar terms this year. Foreign investors have been less interested in Indian equities due to various global factors, and the rupee's depreciation has further amplified losses for overseas investors converting Indian investments.

Meanwhile, the MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbed 0.6% with stocks in Japan and South Korea gaining, following gains for a key gauge of US semiconductor shares.

In other news, Shapoorji Pallonji Group plans to generate $125 million through a tap issue of current dollar bonds, targeting an impressive ₹3,250 crore via unrated rupee-denominated bonds for refinancing purposes.

politics.summary:
The Maharashtra government has unveiled a Fodder Development Policy to tackle a shortage. The policy will include a list of suitable grasses for cultivation, fodder-producing trees, improved fodder crops, and traditional and non-traditional sources of fodder.

The Supreme Court will hear a plea from West Bengal against bail to a Nandigram Congress candidate on October 5.

Chandrababu Naidu has said that the age of AI means that unnecessary regulations must go while government employees keep training.

Congress has sought a discussion on CS and Law Secretary letters in the J&K Assembly, while BJP legislators staged a walkout from the Assembly over the Statehood resolution.

A by-election in Tamil Nadu triggered the first Motion of Confidence in Indian legislature.
